general: This examination consists of multiple sections. You may navigate freely between sections and questions at any time during the examination.
Each question carries the marks indicated alongside it. Read each question carefully before answering.
Your answers will be recorded via dictation. Speak clearly and at a moderate pace for accurate transcription.
Do not attempt to close, minimise, or switch away from this application during the examination.
In case of any technical difficulty, raise your hand to alert the invigilator. Do not attempt to resolve issues yourself.
The examination timer will count down from the total allotted time. When time expires, the examination will be automatically submitted.
You may return to any question to review or revise your answer before submitting.
Once you click 'Submit Exam' and confirm, your answers will be finalised and you cannot make further changes.
examSpecific: This paper covers General Awareness, Essay Writing, and Polity & Governance.
For essay-type questions, structure your answer with an introduction, body paragraphs, and a conclusion.
Answers should be in English unless otherwise specified in the question.
Use factual examples and case studies wherever relevant to substantiate your arguments.
Avoid repeating points across sections — each answer should be self-contained.
instructions.markingScheme: No negative marking. Each question is independently scored. Partial credit may be awarded for well-reasoned incomplete answers at the examiner's discretion.

questions.questionText: India's biodiversity hotspots are regions of significant biological diversity that are threatened by human habitation. Identify any two biodiversity hotspots in India and explain the significance of each.
The Right to Education Act, 2009, mandated free and compulsory education for children. Critically examine the extent to which this act has achieved its intended objectives.
Discuss the socio-economic impacts of digital literacy programs in rural India over the last decade.
Evaluate the role of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in promoting technological advancement and national security.
Analyze the consequences of rapid urbanization on public health infrastructure in metropolitan cities.
The Green Revolution transformed Indian agriculture but generated long-term ecological consequences. Evaluate both the achievements and the unintended consequences.
Examine the role of the Indian Ocean in shaping India's geopolitical strategy in the twenty-first century.
Write an essay on the importance of renewable energy transitions for sustainable economic growth in developing nations.
Discuss the ethical implications of artificial intelligence in governance and public administration.
Analyze the impact of global supply chain disruptions on local economies and strategies for building resilience.
Explain the constitutional provisions that distinguish the powers of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
Discuss the significance of the Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule) in maintaining political stability.
Evaluate the role of the Election Commission of India in ensuring free and fair elections.
Analyze the functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) in empowering local self-governance.
Critically examine the concept of Judicial Review and its impact on the separation of powers in India.
